Title: New programme for direct entrants
NewsSummary: AKU launches a direct entry undergraduate degree in nursing in Tanzania
NewsContent:
The Aga Khan University (AKU) in Tanzania has officially launched the Bachelor of Science in Nursing - Direct Entry programme expected to kick off in November 2023. 

The Tanzania Commission for Universities (TCU) approved the programme attesting to AKU's programmatic growth as it seeks to create leaders in professions and communities from where its students are drawn. 

"We are thrilled to introduce this Bachelor of Science in Nursing in Tanzania. Our two upgrading programmes in nursing and midwifery continue to produce quality nurses who hold strategic leadership positions and influence healthcare policy in the country. To mention a few: Mr Gustav Moyo, Founding Director of Nursing and Midwifery services and Ms Ziada Sellah, current Director of Nursing Services in Tanzania,'' said Dr Eunice Pallangyo, Associate Dean, School of Nursing and Midwifery, East Africa. 

Historically, AKU has been a strong advocate for nursing education not only in Tanzania, but also in Kenya, Uganda, Pakistan, and Afghanistan. As part of this commitment, the University established nursing as its first academic faculty in these countries and has provided vital support to communities by training and educating future nurses and midwives. 

Speaking at the launch event, Chief Guest Dr Edith Rwiza, Director of Human Resource Development at the President's Office of Public Service Management said, "This new programme is particularly exciting because it offers A-level students the opportunity to directly study nursing. This means that more students can now pursue their passion for nursing right after finishing their secondary education. It is a significant step towards expanding access to higher education for the youth of Tanzania and creating more opportunities for them." 

The programme's objective is to offer a nursing education that is rooted in a humanistic approach. AKU aims to nurture nurses who possess not only the necessary clinical skills to provide effective treatment but are also compassionate in delivering high-quality healthcare to patients. Through this approach, the University aspires to produce well-rounded nursing professionals who are equipped to serve their patients holistically and with utmost care. 

"At AKU, our goal is to work with the Government of Tanzania in creating quality market-driven curricula, founded on the Tanzania Development Vision 2025 for 'a well-educated and learning society' and to be a partner in increasing the pool of accessible institutions for higher education for the citizens of the nation. In this journey is our guide the Tanzania Commission for Universities (TCU), its instruments of implementation and the Universities Act Chapter 346 of the Laws of Tanzania, which serve as a beacon on how to contribute to the human capital needs of the nation," said Dr Carl Amrhein, AKU Provost and Vice President, Academic. 

AKU remains committed to supporting the government's agenda of providing accessible and relevant quality education that aligns with the contextual needs of Tanzania. The University's programmes are designed to complement and enhance the government's efforts in improving education and healthcare, thereby contributing to the overall development of the country.
